name: Pixel Wave
author: Wojciech Ratajczak
description: A pixel-block sound visualizer for the bar. Shows a cava spectrum or the loudness of what's playing in seven styles, from a mirrored wave and an equalizer to flames and a pulsing glow, and switches to your microphone in the accent colour while Voxtype records.

barWidget.description: Pixel-block sound visualizer. Left-click switches spectrum and loudness, right-click changes the style.

schema.label: Style
schema.description: mirror is a wave mirrored around a centre line, bars an equalizer rising from the bottom, dots only the outline of the wave, peaks an equalizer with caps that fall back slowly, drip bars hanging from the top, flame bars that fade out at their tips, and pulse a glow in the middle that grows with the volume. Right-clicking the widget cycles them.

schema.label: What it shows
schema.description: spectrum shows frequency bands with the bass in the middle (needs cava); loudness scrolls the volume of what's playing over time. Left-clicking the widget switches them.

schema.label: Pixel size (px)
schema.description: Bigger pixels mean fewer rows fit in the bar.

schema.label: Colour
schema.description: The theme colour the wave is drawn in. The microphone wave uses the accent, or the urgent colour when the wave is already accent.

schema.label: Only on the focused monitor
schema.description: With more than one monitor, show the widget only on the bar of the monitor Hyprland has focused. A single monitor always shows it.

schema.label: Show the microphone while Voxtype records
Hide when nothing is playing
schema.description: Leaves the bar while no application plays sound and the microphone is not shown, instead of resting as a flat line of dots.
